business_problem: As part of its digital-transformation journey, Tapestry has embraced a bold approach to implementing generative AI across its enterprise. Wanting to start with an internal solution before expanding to public applications, the company identified knowledge management as an ideal starting point that would both streamline operations and demonstrate AI's transformative potential.
solution_summary: Tapestry , the global luxury retail company behind iconic brands such as Coach and Kate Spade, spans over 1,400 stores and 18,000 employees worldwide. With business units spread across multiple continents, Tapestry's organizational knowledge was siloed. That made it time-consuming for employees to quickly access critical information and standard operating procedures. To address this challenge, Tapestry used generative artificial intelligence (AI) on Amazon Web Services (AWS) to build an enterprise-wide knowledge management solution that transforms how employees access and interact with company data. In 4 months, Tapestry built, tested, and deployed a knowledge management system that helps employees access and query company information through an intuitive chatbot interface.

solution_components.name: Amazon Bedrock
solution_components.role: Runs the foundation model layer for the knowledge search and question-answering workflows.

solution_components.name: Amazon Titan
solution_components.role: Provides foundation models used inside the knowledge search and question-answering workflows.

solution_components.name: Claude 3 Haiku
solution_components.role: Provides a fast language model used by the knowledge search and question-answering workflows.

data_flow: In 4 months, Tapestry built, tested, and deployed a knowledge management system that helps employees access and query company information through an intuitive chatbot interface. With access to the Claude 3 Haiku large language model through Amazon Bedrock, the solution can also process natural language queries and deliver precise, contextual responses from the company's knowledge base.
business_outcome: Tapestry's knowledge management solution is now being rapidly adopted across the organization. Multiple departments are eager to incorporate their knowledge bases into the new system, and the company is adding new features to enhance the system's capabilities, such as voice interaction.
architecture_clues: In 4 months, Tapestry built, tested, and deployed a knowledge management system that helps employees access and query company information through an intuitive chatbot interface.
The solution uses Amazon Titan foundation models in Amazon Bedrock, which provide a breadth of high-performing image, multimodal, and text model choices.
evidence_quotes: To address this challenge, Tapestry used generative artificial intelligence (AI) on Amazon Web Services (AWS) to build an enterprise-wide knowledge management solution that transforms how employees access and interact with company data.
Tapestry chose AWS to power this solution because of the advanced capabilities available through services such as Amazon Bedrock , which offers a choice of high-performing foundation models.
The solution uses Amazon Titan foundation models in Amazon Bedrock, which provide a breadth of high-performing image, multimodal, and text model choices.

With access to the Claude 3 Haiku large language model through Amazon Bedrock, the solution can also process natural language queries and deliver precise, contextual responses from the company's knowledge base.
It has reduced the time employees spend searching for answers.
"Using generative AI on AWS, we are capturing the DNA of our company," says Aravind Narasimhan, vice president of application technologies at Tapestry.
